Will Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) miss earnings estimates again with itsQ1 earnings on April 27th? Flickr 
Online search giant Google’s parent company Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) is set to report its first quarter 2017earnings on April 27th, after the markets close. The Mountain View, California-based companymissed earnings estimatesin Q4. This miss caused GOOGL stock to plunge by more than 5% post-earnings. As has been the pasttrends, shares of Alphabet Inc have risen sharply ahead of earnings, which have pushed the shares to new all-time highs. GOOGL stock closed at a record close price of $888.84 a share in the last trading session, up by more than 4% in the last 5 trading days alone. The latest all-time highs have resulted in Alphabet rising more than 12% in the YTD. This has been a good run for the internet company after underperforming the market massively in 2016. A major question now is: Will the upcoming earnings send the stock to new highs? The upcomingearnings release will also represent the first time that Alphabetreports only GAAP earnings as opposed to non-GAAP figures. Irrespective of the reporting mechanism, the company needs to beat earnings estimates. Should you buy GOOGL stock going into earnings? Market sentiment was sunny following the release of Warren Buffett’s annual shareholder letter over the weekend, and the Oracle of Omaha made positive comments about the sustainability of the current bull market, which was able to overcome early declines in the major market benchmarks. However, some stocks didn’t fare as well as the overall market, and Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA), AmTrust Financial Services (NASDAQ: AFSI ), and Horizon Pharma (NASDAQ:HZNP) were among the worst performers on the day.
